region.name: Series B Board Prep
region.summary: Leadership materials for the Series B raise and board relations, covering the Northfield Ventures term sheet, diligence timeline, fund pipeline, investor call prep with Granite Peak, board updates, and the VP Engineering search and compensation plan.

brief.text:
Series B Board Prep holds Stencil's leadership materials for the Series B raise and for board and investor relations. The leadership team is CEO Aleks Varga, Maya Chen, Jordan Ellis, Kavi Raman and Renee Alvarez. The anchor document is Northfield Ventures' term sheet: a $38M round at $210M post-money, with Northfield leading up to $32M. The team accepted most terms. Two remain contested: the option pool is to be negotiated, and the team is pushing information rights from monthly to quarterly. The Series B timeline checklist marks several milestones complete, including pitch kickoff, 14 investor meetings, data room v1 and the signed term sheet. Still open are the engineering data room section, the technical diligence call, financial and compliance diligence, legal docs and close. A separate open question asks whether the deck should include quantitative infrastructure metrics such as infrastructure cost as a percentage of revenue and uptime. Aleks favors including them and the author is cautious.

Board updates track operating metrics and milestones. The May 2026 update is the baseline and reports MAU up 22% QoQ. Later updates report 31 engineers out of 64 total staff and progress on the BSA/AML audit and SOC 2. Investing goes to beta at 5% of MTU on Sep 8, subject to Pillar Bank's $2,500 daily funding cap. Other items are Pro Plus Invest pricing, the Lithic card issuing design and a freeze on growth experiments during the beta. The board asks are introductions for the VP Engineering role, warmer Series B intros and a review of compensation philosophy. Stated risks with mitigations are an investing slip, CAC creep and a regulatory surprise, and Maya added a personal note on the April incident. Prep for the 2026-06-04 quarterly call with Dana Whitaker of Granite Peak Capital (Series A lead and board member) set out several goals: get her read on Series B timing, push back on poorly fitting fund matches, pre-flight the investing narrative and align her on VPE compensation. The prep also planned a candid April incident debrief, a Q3 engineering capacity assessment and a clear board ask before kickoff.

The VP Engineering plan pays top-of-band salary with significant equity and avoids signing-bonus games. The hire is targeted 4-6 months after Series B close and will not happen before close. Granite Peak will support intros and reference calls. The search risks are a 9+ month search and poor fit after the hire starts. The sources conflict on recruiting: the comp document says no recruiter will be used, while a board update says the search runs through Hollis Partners. Treat Hollis Partners as the later state, but flag the conflict. Open risks needing attention are a new money-movement incident during diligence (severity 4), Elena probing incident history and asking for evidence (severity 3), the investing feature slipping (severity 3), and Investing GA slipping into November (severity 3, owner Renee Alvarez). An open todo also covers the card issuing design review. Typical questions about this region concern the valuation and round size, which terms are being negotiated, diligence status, how to frame the April incident, investing beta and GA timing, and VPE hiring terms.

items.title: Decision: Pay top-of-band or over-band for VPE
items.summary: Intent to pay top-of-band, possibly over-band, for the right VPE candidate; Aleks is sympathetic but cost-conscious.
